name: Mandarin Oriental Residences Saadiyat Cultural District, Abu Dhabi

fields.description: This Aldar residential development occupies a setting beside the Zayed National Museum in Saadiyat Cultural District. Its 226 furnished residences were designed by Bjarke Ingels Group, with interiors by Lillian Wu and residential management announced with Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group.

sources.label: Aldar: Mandarin Oriental Residences launch, 15 November 2024
Aldar: residence presentation, layouts and original schedule

reviewCoverage.identity: Own Aldar page, November 2024 launch and official presentation reviewed; separate older hotel proposals excluded.
reviewCoverage.location: Saadiyat Cultural District and Zayed National Museum setting confirmed.

reviewCoverage.areas: Page 25 average-area and balcony columns visually inspected; averages are not individual unit sizes.

overview: The announced design combines furnished homes, natural marble, warm timber and carefully considered lighting. Open living areas connect with kitchens and terraces. The branded service proposition is separate from the developer’s ownership and sales role; buyers should review the current management and service documents alongside the home specification.
research.locationNote: The official launch describes a position overlooking the Zayed National Museum and its fountains, with access to Saadiyat’s cultural destinations and Mamsha Beach. A residence’s exact view depends on its tower, floor and orientation.
research.priceNote: The presentation lists average prices: AED 6.2m for one bedroom, 12.2m for two, 16.6m for two plus maid, 25.2m for three plus maid and 42.1m for large three-bedroom pool homes. These are not live offers.
research.paymentNote: The original dated schedule totals 65% before handover and 35% at completion. Reconfirm current terms.
research.handoverNote: The presentation estimates Q3 2028. The contract governs possession.

facts.label: Design team
facts.value: Aldar’s launch names Bjarke Ingels Group as architect and Lillian Wu as interior designer. Furniture and finishing commitments still need checking against the selected unit’s signed specification.
